reference.source: Paley, Manual of Gothic Mouldings 1845, Plate I fig 7 (leaf n88): three receding orders 1.4 x 1.4 with a quarter-round hollow struck in every re-entrant angle. PROPORTIONAL ONLY - fig 7 carries no dimension line (recorded); component bbox plate x[1230,1484] y[595,889]
reference.source_frame: relative construction; the recorded built extent 5.05 x 5.9 matches the plate component bbox ratio (254/294 px) and is adopted here as the outline's extent claims

construction_plane.profile_x: +X along the outer wall-line, orders receding

arris1.note: salient arris of the first order

cove1_in.note: cove tangent on the riser, 0.85 above the re-entrant corner; 0.55 of flat riser remains

cove3_out.note: the drawing's component bbox ends at the third cove's exit (x=5.05); the innermost plane continues beyond the drawn crop, so the closure turns down here. The exit tangency to horizontal remains a fact of the centre placement

segments.note: quarter hollow struck in the first re-entrant angle, tangent to riser and tread; centre sits in the void

notes: THE FAITHFUL FIG 7 - upgrades stepped_paley_pl1_fig7_v1 (which deliberately omitted the hollows as the straight-only stress variant). Paley's vocabulary contrast case: no chamfer-plane member at all; mouldings developed by sinking hollows in the wall- and soffit-planes only.

Cove reading validated by the record itself: tangent quarter-hollows 0.85 into each re-entrant angle put the rightmost moulded point at exactly x = 4.2 + 0.85 = 5.05 - the recorded built extent width.

Old-workflow defects, quantified: its builder yields extent 4.2 x 3.35 with endpoint (3.35,-3.35), against its own record's 5.05 x 5.9 - not internally reproducible; heading contamination rotates each successive hollow (chord of hollow 1: (2.25,0.85); hollow 2: (0.55,-0.61)) where the plate shows three identical hollows.
Five SMOOTH joins verified by the compiler - the heaviest tangency load of any profile yet. All three coves are identical translates, as drawn.
Traversal is CLOCKWISE with solid RIGHT (stone below-left of the descending orders), the same layout as the stepped variant for comparability.
